summary: Carroll County tower named on 1968 and 2010 Hillsville topo sheets; the Association lists it gone, and the 2010 description says it stands.

facts.status_note: The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it as gone. A 2010 map description calls it a standing landmark. No source describes the site now.

evidence.supports: Association lists Longshoal, Carroll County, at 36.87143, -80.71913 as a tower, gone
1968 survey names the Longshoal Lookout Tower as a notable high point above the creek valleys
evidence.quote: Notable high points such as Longshoal Lookout Tower and Witcher Knob stand above the creek valleys

evidence.supports: Hillsville anchors the southwest corner of the late-1960s survey
evidence.quote: Hillsville anchors the southwest corner of this late-1960s survey

evidence.supports: Map is a USGS topographic sheet
2010 description says the tower stands as a prominent landmark on the northern ridge
evidence.quote: the Longshoal Lookout Tower stands as a prominent landmark on the northern ridge

evidence.supports: Map is a USGS topographic sheet

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Association lists the tower as gone; the 2010 Pastmaps description says it stands. A map description does not date a structure, so the story reports both and does not settle the status.

notes_for_editor: Only the FFLA list and two map-page descriptions mention the tower. Build date, design, staffing, access and removal are not described in any source found. The easternuslookouts.weebly.com Virginia page has a LONGSHOAL heading with a photo (/uploads/1/5/9/1/1591048/9874261_orig.png) and no licence or description; not added. The anyplaceamerica.com page returned 403 and the getamap.net page is auto-generated, so neither is cited. The 2010 map description conflicts with the FFLA gone entry; a human should check current aerial imagery or a visit before changing status.
